description: Marine wave and ocean conditions for a coastal or ocean coordinate: wave height, wave period, wave direction, wind-wave height, swell height, sea-surface temperature. Forecast horizon up to 8 days, with optional past_days (up to 92) for recent history — or start_date and end_date together for an archive range, which returns real wave values back to at least 2022. One window per call: a date range is mutually exclusive with forecast_days and past_days, and needs both ends — a lone start_date or end_date is rejected. Returns per-timestamp records — each entry contains a "time" field plus one key per requested variable. Best for open-ocean and coastal exposed points — sheltered water such as a sound or bay returns near-zero wave values, and a land point returns null values, which the notice reports. Common hourly variables: wave_height, wave_direction, wave_period, wind_wave_height, wind_wave_direction, wind_wave_period, swell_wave_height, swell_wave_direction, swell_wave_period. Common daily: wave_height_max, wave_direction_dominant, wave_period_max. Note: ocean_current_velocity is null for non-open-ocean coordinates. Set current_variables for conditions at this instant — Open-Meteo serves those from 15-minute model data, and the response carries a current object plus a current_units map, alongside either window. length_unit "imperial" returns heights in ft, wind_speed_unit sets the ocean_current_velocity unit, and temperature_unit the sea_surface_temperature unit — converted upstream, with every unit read from the *_units maps. A wide window — a large past_days or date range plus many variables — produces thousands of records; these spill to a DataCanvas when canvas is enabled, returning canvas_id and table_name with truncated: true — inspect the staged columns with openmeteo_dataframe_describe, then query the full set with openmeteo_dataframe_query. With canvas disabled they return a bounded preview instead. At least one of current_variables, hourly_variables, or daily_variables is required.

canvas_id.description: DataCanvas token for wide past_days, archive-range, or multi-variable queries. When a result is too large to return inline — driven by total payload size, so a wide multi-variable pull can spill at any row count — it spills to this canvas: pass the returned token to openmeteo_dataframe_describe to list the staged table and its columns, then to openmeteo_dataframe_query to run SQL against it. Omit to create a fresh canvas.

current_variables.description: Marine variables to return for the current instant (e.g., ["wave_height", "wave_period", "wave_direction", "sea_surface_temperature"]). Uses Open-Meteo's 15-minute current-conditions data, so it answers "what are the waves right now?" without requesting an hourly series and picking a row. Takes the hourly variable names — a daily aggregate such as wave_height_max belongs in daily_variables and is rejected here. Combines with past_days or a start_date/end_date range; the current block is always the present instant. Satisfies the variable requirement on its own.

daily_variables.description: Daily marine summary variables (e.g., ["wave_height_max", "wave_direction_dominant", "wave_period_max"]). Daily names only — an hourly name such as wave_height belongs in hourly_variables and is rejected here; for a daily summary use its published aggregate (wave_height_max). At least one of current_variables, hourly_variables, or daily_variables is required.

end_date.description: End date for the archive range (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive). Must be on or after start_date. Requires start_date — the pair must be sent together, and neither combines with forecast_days or past_days.

forecast_days.description: Forecast horizon in days (1–8). Omit for the upstream default of 7. Mutually exclusive with start_date/end_date — omit it entirely when pulling an archive range.

hourly_variables.description: Hourly marine variables (e.g., ["wave_height", "wave_direction", "wave_period", "wind_wave_height", "swell_wave_height"]). Hourly names only — a daily aggregate such as wave_height_max or wave_direction_dominant belongs in daily_variables and is rejected here. At least one of current_variables, hourly_variables, or daily_variables is required.

latitude.description: Latitude of a coastal or ocean point. Use openmeteo_search_locations to resolve a place name. Sheltered water returns near-zero wave values; a land point returns null values, which the notice reports.

length_unit.description: Unit for wave, wind-wave, and swell heights and sea_level_height_msl: "metric" (m) or "imperial" (ft). Periods stay in seconds and directions in degrees. Default "metric".

past_days.description: Include this many days of past data before today (0–92). Use for recent history instead of a start_date/end_date range. Default 0. Must stay 0 when start_date/end_date are used.

start_date.description: Start date for the archive range (YYYY-MM-DD, e.g., "2024-07-01"). Real wave values go back to at least 2022. Requires end_date — the pair must be sent together, and neither combines with forecast_days or past_days.

wind_speed_unit.description: Unit for ocean_current_velocity: "kmh" (km/h), "mph" (labelled "mp/h" in the units maps), "ms" (m/s), or "kn" (knots). Default "kmh".

name: openmeteo_get_marine

canvas_id.description: DataCanvas token for the staged full dataset. Present only when truncated is true AND DataCanvas is enabled (CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE=duckdb) — absent otherwise, in which case the preview is all this response carries. Pass to openmeteo_dataframe_describe to list the staged table and its columns, then to openmeteo_dataframe_query to run SQL against it.

current.description: Conditions at a single instant: one key per requested current variable alongside time and interval. Units are in the current_units map. Absent when current_variables was not requested.

interval.description: Aggregation interval of the current block, in seconds (900 = 15 minutes on this endpoint) — metadata, not a requested variable. The marine variables are instantaneous, so each value is valid at current.time

time.description: Timestamp of these values (ISO 8601, in the resolved timezone)

current_units.description: Key → unit string for the current block, covering time and interval as well as each requested variable (e.g., {"interval": "seconds", "wave_height": "ft"}). Absent when no current_variables were requested.

daily.description: Per-day summary records with "time" (YYYY-MM-DD) + variable keys (e.g., wave_height_max, wave_direction_dominant, wave_period_max). Units are in the daily_units map; heights follow length_unit. Absent when only hourly_variables were requested. When truncated, contains only a preview — query canvas_id for the full dataset when one is present.

daily_units.description: Variable → unit string for daily data. Absent when no daily_variables were requested.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_variable`: An unknown marine variable name was requested. `variable_wrong_cadence`: A variable sat in a field Open-Meteo does not document it under — for example wave_height in daily_variables, or wave_height_max in hourly_variables or current_variables — caught before the request is sent. `no_variables_requested`: None of current_variables, hourly_variables, or daily_variables named a variable — blank or whitespace-only entries do not count. `date_range_incomplete`: Only one of start_date / end_date was provided — the marine archive requires the pair together. `forecast_window_conflict`: A start_date or end_date range was combined with forecast_days or a non-zero past_days value. `date_order_invalid`: The end_date value is earlier than the start_date value. `invalid_timezone`: timezone was blank, or upstream did not recognize the requested time zone. `request_too_large`: Open-Meteo refused the request as asking for too much data in one call. `coverage_gap`: Open-Meteo has no data at this coordinate for the requested dataset or model, because its grid or domain does not reach the point. `rate_limited`: Open-Meteo answered HTTP 429 because a free-tier request limit was reached. `upstream_unavailable`: Open-Meteo was unreachable, answered with a server error, or returned an unreadable response on all three attempts. `upstream_timeout`: Open-Meteo failed on all three attempts, and the last one got no answer within 15 seconds. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

hourly.description: Per-hour records with "time" (ISO 8601) + one key per requested variable (e.g., wave_height, wave_direction, wave_period). Units are in the hourly_units map: heights follow length_unit, ocean_current_velocity follows wind_speed_unit, sea_surface_temperature follows temperature_unit. Absent when only daily_variables were requested. When truncated, contains only a preview — query canvas_id for the full dataset when one is present.

hourly_units.description: Variable → unit string for hourly data, as Open-Meteo labels it (e.g., {"wave_height": "ft", "wave_period": "s"} under length_unit "imperial"). Absent when no hourly_variables were requested.

notice.description: Everything this response needs to say beyond the data, composed into one advisory: columns the endpoint returned with the unit "undefined" (a name it parsed but does not serve); current values that are null under a real unit (no coverage at this location, such as a land point); recognized variables whose requested window or location falls outside the data's coverage (a land point returns nulls), with the timestamps that do carry values; and, when the result spilled, either the canvas and table holding the full row set plus the two dataframe tools that read it, or — with DataCanvas disabled — why there is no canvas_id and how to reach the rows the preview omits.

record_count.description: Total number of records (hourly + daily rows) — the full upstream total when truncated is true, not the combined length of the hourly and daily previews.

table_name.description: DuckDB table name for the staged data — use as the FROM target in openmeteo_dataframe_query SQL; openmeteo_dataframe_describe lists its columns. Present only alongside canvas_id.

truncated.description: True when the response was too large to return inline, so hourly and daily carry a bounded preview rather than the full set. With DataCanvas enabled the complete data is staged at canvas_id — every hourly and daily row, including any column the preview omits. With it disabled there is no canvas_id, and the omitted rows are reached only by narrowing the request.
